newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronics tumble on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronics tumble on profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan's electronic shares fell at mid-session on Wednesday as investors took profits against the sector's big recent gains, switching funds into recently lagging shares, brokers said.

With 60 minutes left in the session at 0300 GMT, the electronics index had slumped 4.54 percent, with Taiwan's top chipmaker, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, tumbling by the daily seven-percent limit or T$8.50 to T$115.
Another chip giant, United Microelectronics, fell 6.17 percent or T$7 to T$106.50.
Both Taiwan Semiconductor and United Micro recently had soared on announcements that both planned to build huge microchip plants in the southern Tainan science park.
"The electronics have simply risen too much recently, and investors feel it is time to transfer some of their money into cheaper shares," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.
One of benefactor of the electronic sell-off was the construction sector, which was up 3.18 percent.
The overall index, which gained more than 10 percent in June, was up 0.36 percent or 32.65 points at 9,062.93.
